examples.ko: 이 벽지는 하얀색보다 아이보리가 더 따뜻해 보여요.
examples.en: On this wallpaper, ivory looks warmer than white.
I bought an ivory-colored coat.
I often mix up ivory and beige.
After changing the curtains to ivory, the room felt cozy.

examples.ko: 아이보리 소파 위에 강아지가 올라가 있어요.
examples.en: A puppy is up on the ivory sofa.

examples.ko: 아이보리 같은 밝은 색은 때가 잘 타요.
examples.en: Light colors like ivory get dirty easily.

explain: 한국에서는 '흰색'과 '베이지' 사이의 색을 영어 그대로 '아이보리'라고 해요. 옷, 가구, 벽지 색을 말할 때 많이 나오고, 흰색보다 부드럽고 따뜻한 느낌이에요. '아이보리색'처럼 '색'을 붙여도 돼요.

phrases.en: I wore an ivory-colored blouse.
phrases.nuance_ko: '색'을 붙여 옷이나 물건의 색을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '색' is used to state the color of clothes or objects.

phrases.en: I decorated the room in ivory tones.
phrases.nuance_ko: 인테리어나 화장품 이야기에서 전체 분위기를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used in interior or makeup talk for an overall color mood.

phrases.en: I painted the wall ivory.
phrases.nuance_ko: 색을 고르거나 바꿀 때는 '-로'와 같이 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use '-로' when choosing or changing to a color.

explain_en: In Korean the color between '흰색' and '베이지' is called '아이보리', the English word kept as is. It comes up a lot for clothes, furniture, and wallpaper, and feels softer and warmer than white. You can also add '색', as in '아이보리색'.

examples.en: Under the moonlight the lake sparkles silver.
The grandmother with silvery hair is smiling.
The fish's scales are silver.

examples.ko: 그 배우는 은빛 드레스를 입고 나왔어요.
examples.en: The actress appeared in a silver dress.
A silvery field of snow spread out on the winter morning.
Silver feels calmer than gold.

explain: 은빛은 반짝이는 은색 빛이라서 달빛, 눈, 물결, 흰머리를 예쁘게 표현할 때 좋아요. 짝이 되는 말은 '금빛'이에요. 흰머리를 멋지게 말할 때는 '은발'이라고도 해요.

phrases.en: Silvery waves sparkle on the sea.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물에 비친 빛을 예쁘게 표현할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A pretty way to describe light on water.

phrases.en: The snow-covered mountain shines silver.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-으로'를 붙여 어떤 색으로 빛나는지 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: -으로 says what color it shines.

phrases.en: A silvery moon hangs in the night sky.
phrases.nuance_ko: 밝고 차가운 달빛을 시처럼 표현할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A poetic way to describe bright, cool moonlight.

explain_en: Silver light or shine on things like the moon (은빛 달) 은빛 is silver with a shimmer, so it suits moonlight, snow, ripples, and gray hair. Its counterpart is 금빛. Gray hair can also be called 은발 in a flattering way.

examples.en: She wrapped a rose-colored scarf around her head.
The evening sky turned rosy.
The baby's cheeks are flushed and rosy.
I worked hard, dreaming of a rosy future.
But reality wasn't rosy.
A pretty rose-pink petal fell.

explain: '분홍빛'보다 장미꽃처럼 붉은 기가 도는 연한 색을 말해요. 색깔 외에 '밝고 희망적인'이라는 비유로도 많이 써요. 발음은 [장미삗]이에요.

phrases.example: 졸업만 하면 장밋빛 미래가 펼쳐질 줄 알았어요.
phrases.en: I thought a rosy future would open up once I graduated.
phrases.nuance_ko: 실제 색이 아니라 앞날이 매우 밝고 희망차다는 뜻이에요. 현실은 그렇지 않다는 말과 같이 쓰일 때가 많아요.
phrases.nuance_en: It does not refer to an actual color but to a bright, hopeful future. It is often used together with the idea that reality isn't that way.

explain_en: Compared with '분홍빛' (pink), it points to a light color with a red tint, like a rose. Beyond color it is often used figuratively for 'bright and hopeful'. It is pronounced [장미삗].

examples.en: With autumn, the leaves turned reddish brown.
I bought a reddish-brown leather bag.
My hair looks reddish brown in the sunlight.

examples.ko: 이 소파는 적갈색이라서 방이 따뜻해 보여요.
examples.en: This sofa is reddish brown, so the room looks warm.
The house built with reddish-brown bricks is pretty.
The soil has a reddish-brown tint.

explain: 붉은빛이 도는 갈색이에요. 일상에서는 '붉은 갈색'이나 '밤색'처럼 말할 때도 많아요. '~색을 띠다'와 함께 자주 나와요. 발음은 [적깔쌕]이에요.

phrases.en: This soil has a reddish-brown color.
phrases.nuance_ko: 색깔이 그렇게 보인다고 설명할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to describe that something appears in this color.

phrases.en: I like chestnut-brown shoes.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상에서 더 쉽게 쓰는 갈색 계열 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easier everyday word for a chestnut-brown shade.

phrases.en: I dyed my hair reddish brown.
phrases.nuance_ko: '적갈색'을 쉬운 말로 풀어서 말한 거예요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easier way of saying 적갈색.

explain_en: Reddish brown like rust or autumn leaves, slightly formal. It is a brown with a red tint. In daily talk people also say '붉은 갈색' or '밤색'. It often appears with '~색을 띠다'. It is pronounced [적깔쌕].

t90.ax: The soil has a reddish-brown tint.

examples.en: This blanket feels really soft to the touch.

examples.ko: 이 천은 촉감은 좋지만 빨면 줄어들어요.
examples.en: This fabric feels nice, but it shrinks when washed.

examples.ko: 눈을 감고 촉감만으로 물건을 맞혀 보세요.
examples.en: Close your eyes and guess the object by touch alone.

examples.ko: 강아지 털의 촉감을 잊을 수 없어요.
examples.en: I can't forget the feel of the puppy's fur.

examples.ko: 촉감 때문에 이 스웨터는 입기 불편해요.
examples.en: This sweater is uncomfortable to wear because of how it feels.

examples.ko: 종이의 촉감에 따라 책 느낌이 달라져요.
examples.en: The feel of a book changes with the feel of its paper.

explain: '촉감이 좋다', '촉감이 거칠다', '촉감이 부드럽다'처럼 말해요. 옷감, 이불, 화장품, 종이를 이야기할 때 자주 나와요. 비슷한 '감촉'도 거의 같은 뜻으로 바꿔 쓸 수 있어요.

phrases.en: This towel feels soft to the touch.
phrases.nuance_ko: '촉감'과 거의 같은 뜻으로 바꿔 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Nearly interchangeable with 촉감.

phrases.en: This paper feels rough.
phrases.nuance_ko: 만졌을 때 매끄럽지 않은 느낌을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes something that doesn't feel smooth to touch.

phrases.en: In summer, clothes that feel nice are comfortable.
phrases.nuance_ko: '촉감이 좋은' 뒤에 옷, 이불, 천 같은 물건을 붙여 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put items like clothes, blankets, or fabric after '촉감이 좋은'.

explain_en: Physical feel of a surface against skin: soft, rough, smooth (촉감이 부드럽다). Say '촉감이 좋다', '촉감이 거칠다', or '촉감이 부드럽다'. It comes up often for fabric, bedding, cosmetics, and paper. The similar '감촉' can be swapped in with almost the same meaning.

en: being covered in dirt; a muddy mess

examples.ko: 비가 온 뒤라 길이 흙투성이로 지저분해졌어요.
examples.en: After the rain, the road got dirty and covered with mud.
I came back from playing soccer and my clothes are covered in dirt.
The puppy came back covered in mud.
Please leave muddy shoes outside the entrance.
Grandma's hands were covered in dirt after finishing the field work.

examples.ko: 넘어진 아이의 무릎이 흙투성이라 씻겨 줬어요.
examples.en: The fallen child's knee was caked with dirt, so I washed it.

explain: '~투성이'는 어떤 것이 온통 묻어 있다는 뜻으로 '먼지투성이', '땀투성이', '피투성이'처럼 대체로 지저분하거나 좋지 않은 것에 붙여요. 항상 붙여 쓰고, '흙투성이가 되다'로 많이 말해요.

phrases.en: I got covered in mud all over while playing ball.
phrases.nuance_ko: '흙투성이가 되다'는 온통 흙이 묻은 상태로 바뀔 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: '흙투성이가 되다' is used when something becomes covered all over with dirt.

phrases.en: I washed my muddy shoes.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 앞에서 꾸며 주는 말로 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Can be placed before a noun to describe it.

phrases.en: The child came home covered in dirt.
phrases.nuance_ko: '로'를 붙여 어떤 상태로 왔는지 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adds '로' to say in what condition someone came.

explain_en: The suffix '~투성이' means covered all over with something, and it is usually attached to unpleasant things, as in '먼지투성이', '땀투성이' and '피투성이'. It is always written without a space, and '흙투성이가 되다' is a common pattern.

en: to be loving; to be caring

examples.en: My grandmother always speaks in a warm, kind voice.

examples.ko: 두 사람이 다정스럽게 손을 잡고 걸어요.
examples.en: The two of them walk hand in hand affectionately.

examples.ko: 새로 온 선생님이 다정스러워서 학생들이 좋아해요.
examples.en: The new teacher is warm, so the students like her.

examples.ko: 옆집 아저씨는 다정스럽지는 않지만 마음이 따뜻해요.
examples.en: The man next door is not affectionate, but he has a warm heart.
The way he held the child looked so tender.

examples.ko: 다정스러운 말 한마디에 하루가 달라질 때가 있어요.
examples.en: Sometimes one kind word can change your whole day.

explain: '다정하다'와 뜻이 거의 같고, '-스럽다'가 붙어 그런 분위기나 태도가 느껴진다는 뜻이 더해져요. 사람의 말투, 표정, 모습을 꾸며 줄 때 어울려요. ㅂ불규칙이라 '다정스러워요', '다정스러운'으로 바뀌어요.

phrases.en: Mom called me in a loving voice.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 앞에서 꾸며 주는 활용형이에요. 말투나 목소리가 따뜻하게 느껴질 때 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: The form that modifies a noun, fitting when a tone or voice feels warm.

phrases.en: The teacher spoke to the students affectionately.
phrases.nuance_ko: 동사를 꾸며 주는 부사형이에요. 행동이나 말하는 방식을 설명할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The adverb form that modifies a verb, used to describe how someone acts or speaks.

phrases.en: The two of them are really affectionate.
phrases.nuance_ko: '다정스럽다'의 해요체예요. ㅂ불규칙이라 '다정스러워요'로 바뀌어요.
phrases.nuance_en: The polite 해요 form of '다정스럽다', changing to '다정스러워요' because it is ㅂ-irregular.

explain_en: It means almost the same as '다정하다', and the '-스럽다' ending adds the sense that the warmth can be felt in someone's manner. It fits a person's voice, expression, or look. It is a ㅂ-irregular adjective, so it becomes '다정스러워요' and '다정스러운'.

en: in affectionate whispers; with affectionate murmuring

examples.en: The family gathers and chats in warm, quiet voices.
I can hear soft, friendly voices from the kitchen.

examples.ko: 친구와 도란도란 얘기하다 보니 시간이 훌쩍 갔어요.
examples.en: Chatting cozily with my friend, the time flew by.
I listened to old stories next to my grandmother in a cozy, quiet way.

examples.ko: 아이들이 이불 속에서 도란도란 속삭이고 있어요.
examples.en: The children are whispering cozily under the blanket.
Shall we talk quietly as we walk?

explain: '소곤소곤'은 작은 목소리에 초점이 있지만, '도란도란'은 정답고 화목한 분위기까지 담겨 있어요. 보통 '이야기하다, 말하다, 속삭이다' 같은 말과 함께 써요. 싸우거나 긴장된 대화에는 어울리지 않아요.

phrases.example: 저녁에 가족과 도란도란 이야기하며 밥을 먹어요.
phrases.en: In the evening I eat while chatting warmly with my family.
phrases.nuance_ko: 정답게 이야기하는 모습에 가장 많이 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing for chatting warmly.

phrases.en: The children whisper cozily in bed.
phrases.nuance_ko: 작은 목소리로 다정하게 말하는 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Gives a feeling of speaking softly and affectionately.

phrases.en: In the library, we speak in whispers.
phrases.nuance_ko: 작은 목소리에 초점이 있고, 정다운 분위기는 꼭 없어도 돼요.
phrases.nuance_en: Focuses on a small voice and doesn't need a warm mood.

explain_en: '소곤소곤' focuses on a small voice, but '도란도란' also carries a warm, friendly mood. It usually goes with verbs like '이야기하다', '말하다' and '속삭이다'. It doesn't suit an argument or a tense conversation.

en: to put arms around each other's shoulders

examples.en: We walked home with our arms around each other's shoulders.

examples.ko: 아이들이 어깨동무해서 한 줄로 서 있어요.
examples.en: The kids stand in a line with their arms over each other's shoulders.

examples.ko: 친한 친구끼리 어깨동무하면 사진이 더 정다워 보여요.
examples.en: When close friends put their arms around each other, the photo looks warmer.
We sang the cheer song with our arms around each other.
After we put our arms around each other, we felt closer.
It's embarrassing to put an arm around someone you've just met.

explain: '어깨동무를 하다'를 한 단어처럼 쓴 말이에요. 서로 어깨에 팔을 두르는 것이라서, 팔을 끼는 '팔짱을 끼다'와 구분해서 써요.

phrases.en: My friend and I put our arms around each other's shoulders when taking the photo.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지난 일을 말하는 해요체 과거형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The polite past tense, used to talk about something that already happened.
phrases.en_equiv: put arms around each other's shoulders (past)

phrases.en: Let's put our arms around each other!
phrases.nuance_ko: 친한 친구에게 하는 반말 권유 표현이에요. 윗사람에게는 쓰지 않아요.
phrases.nuance_en: A casual suggestion to close friends. Don't use it with someone older or senior.
phrases.en_equiv: let's put our arms around each other

phrases.en: The kids sing with their arms around each other's shoulders.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-고'로 이어서 다른 동작을 함께 하는 쓰임이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The -고 ending connects it to another action done at the same time.
phrases.en_equiv: to sing with arms around each other's shoulders

explain_en: It is '어깨동무를 하다' used as a single verb. It means two people put arms around each other's shoulders, which is different from '팔짱을 끼다', linking arms.

examples.en: A goddess of love appears in Greek mythology.

examples.ko: 이 동상은 바다의 여신을 만든 거예요.
examples.en: This statue depicts the goddess of the sea.

examples.ko: 여신 같은 분위기의 배우가 무대에 나왔어요.
examples.en: An actress with a goddess-like aura came onto the stage.
Fans call that singer a goddess.
People prayed to the goddess of a good harvest.
The children enjoy reading stories about goddesses.

explain: 남신은 남자 신이고 '여신'은 여자 신이에요. 신화에서 쓰지만 요즘은 아주 아름답거나 인기가 많은 여성을 칭찬하는 말로도 많이 써요. 이때는 '여신 미모'처럼 가볍게 말해요.

phrases.en: That actress looks like a goddess.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아주 아름다운 여성을 칭찬하는 가벼운 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A casual compliment for a very beautiful woman.

phrases.en: A large statue of a goddess stands by the sea.
phrases.nuance_ko: '상'을 붙이면 여신을 본떠 만든 조각이라는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '상' means a statue made in the image of a goddess.

phrases.en: Today the goddess of victory was on our side.
phrases.nuance_ko: '~의 여신'은 신화 속 여신뿐 아니라 운이 좋았다는 표현에도 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: 'Goddess of ~' is used for mythical goddesses and also for saying luck was on your side.

explain_en: A male deity is 남신 and a female deity is 여신. It is used in myths, but these days it is also a common compliment for a very beautiful or popular woman, as in '여신 미모'.

en: to be righteous; to be morally just

examples.en: He is a just police officer.
I want to build a just society.
The way they helped their friend is righteous.
Acting justly is not easy.
I think a person looks coolest when they are righteous.
He is just, so many people trust and follow him.

explain: '정의'에 '-롭다'가 붙은 말로 ㅂ 불규칙이라 '정의로워요', '정의로운'으로 바뀌어요. 사람이나 행동, 사회를 칭찬할 때 써요. 일상 대화보다 글이나 영화 이야기에서 더 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: I want to be a righteous person.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람 앞에서 꾸며 주는 가장 기본 형태예요.
phrases.nuance_en: The basic form used before a noun to describe a person.

phrases.en: The main character of that movie is really righteous.
phrases.nuance_ko: ㅂ 불규칙 형용사라서 '정의로워요'로 바뀌어요.
phrases.nuance_en: It is a ㅂ-irregular adjective, so it becomes 정의로워요.

phrases.en: That decision is not just.
phrases.nuance_ko: 옳지 않다고 비판할 때 쓰는 부정 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Negative form used to criticize something as unfair.

explain_en: Built from the noun for justice plus a suffix, it is a b-irregular adjective, so it becomes the forms ending in 'wo'. It praises people, actions and societies, and shows up more in writing and movie talk than in daily chat.

dis.h: morally right, standing up for justice

p.n: '정의롭다' is morally righteous and brave about right and wrong; '공정하다' is fair-minded and unbiased.

examples.en: This day is commemorated every year.
That event is commemorated at the museum.
Today is a day when the founding is commemorated.

examples.ko: 영웅이 기념될 수 있도록 동상을 세웠어요.
examples.en: They put up a statue so the hero can be remembered.
The commemorated date is written on the calendar.
It was commemorated with an event, so many people came.

explain: 기념일이나 큰 일을 기억하고 축하하는 행사가 있을 때 써요. 사람이 하면 '기념하다', 날이나 사건이 주인이면 '기념되다'예요. 일상 대화에서는 '기념일', '기념품', '기념사진'처럼 명사로 더 많이 써요.

phrases.en: Today is our school's anniversary.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기억하고 축하하는 특별한 날을 말하는 명사예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A noun for a special day that is remembered and celebrated.

phrases.en: We took a commemorative photo at the graduation.
phrases.nuance_ko: 특별한 날을 기억하려고 찍는 사진이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A photo taken to remember a special day.

phrases.en: We ate cake to celebrate the birthday.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람이 주어일 때는 '기념하다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use 기념하다 when a person is the subject.

explain_en: Used when a special day or big event is remembered with a ceremony. A person doing it uses the active verb; the day or event as subject takes this passive. In daily talk the noun forms like anniversary, souvenir and commemorative photo are more common.

examples.en: My mother sings in the church choir.
The choir practices every Sunday morning.

examples.ko: 성가대 옷을 입은 아이들이 줄을 섰어요.
examples.en: The children in choir robes lined up.
The choir's song at the Christmas service was moving.
I also want to join the choir.
A new choir conductor has arrived.

explain: 교회나 성당에서만 쓰는 말이에요. 학교나 동네 모임은 '합창단'이라고 해요. '성가대에서 노래하다', '성가대 연습'처럼 써요.

phrases.en: My younger sibling is a church choir member.
phrases.nuance_ko: 성가대에서 노래하는 한 사람을 가리켜요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to one person who sings in the choir.

phrases.en: I joined the church choir this time too.
phrases.nuance_ko: 새로 가입할 때 쓰는 자연스러운 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A natural phrase for joining newly.

phrases.en: The choir conductor teaches us the songs.
phrases.nuance_ko: 성가대를 이끄는 사람을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the person who leads the choir.

explain_en: Organized group singing hymns, at church or school. It is used only for churches and cathedrals. A school or community group is a 합창단. You say 성가대에서 노래하다 or 성가대 연습.

examples.en: I saw a large oil painting at the art museum.
She paints oil paintings every weekend.

examples.ko: 유화는 마르는 데 시간이 오래 걸려요.
examples.en: Oil paintings take a long time to dry.

examples.ko: 아버지가 거실에 유화 한 점을 걸었어요.
examples.en: My father hung an oil painting in the living room.
The smell of oil paint spread through the room.
Oil painting is harder for me than watercolor.

explain: 그림 종류는 '유화'와 '수채화'를 같이 외우면 좋아요. 유화는 기름 물감으로 두껍게 그리는 그림이고, 수채화는 물을 섞어 연하게 그려요.

phrases.example: 유화 물감은 마르는 데 시간이 오래 걸려요.
phrases.en: Oil paint takes a long time to dry.
phrases.nuance_ko: 유화를 그릴 때 쓰는 기름 물감을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The oil-based paint used to make oil paintings.

phrases.example: 거실에 유화 한 점을 걸어 두었어요.
phrases.en: I hung one oil painting in the living room.
phrases.nuance_ko: 그림을 셀 때는 '점'이라는 단위를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The counter 점 is used to count artworks.

phrases.en: I painted this landscape in oils.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어떤 방법으로 그렸는지 말할 때 '-로'를 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add -로 to say which medium was used.

explain_en: Painting made with oil paints; art technique (유화) It helps to learn 유화 together with 수채화. 유화 is thick painting in oil paint, while 수채화 is light painting mixed with water.

examples.ko: 주사위를 던져서 나온 수만큼 말을 움직여요.
examples.en: You throw the dice and move your piece by the number that comes up.
The die rolled off onto the floor.
We decided the order with a die instead of rock-paper-scissors.

examples.ko: 보드게임에서 주사위 두 개를 같이 굴려요.
examples.en: In the board game, you roll two dice together.

examples.ko: 주사위에는 일부터 육까지 점이 찍혀 있어요.
examples.en: A die has dots from one to six on it.
I had good luck with the dice this time.

explain: '주사위를 던지다/굴리다'로 말하고, 점이 찍힌 면은 '눈'이라고 해서 '눈이 6이 나왔다'처럼 말해요. 정하기 어려울 때 '주사위를 던져서 정하자'고도 해요.

phrases.en: the die is cast
phrases.nuance_ko: 이미 결정을 했고 돌이킬 수 없다는 뜻이에요. 큰 결정을 하고 나서 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: It means a decision has been made and cannot be reversed. People use it after a big decision.

explain_en: People say '주사위를 던지다/굴리다' (throw/roll the dice), and the dotted faces are called '눈', so you say '눈이 6이 나왔다' (a six came up). When a choice is hard, people also say '주사위를 던져서 정하자' (let's decide by dice).
